checks: Independently counted the lattice points by oriented triangle-edge determinants. The 31 sites have parity counts (10,7,7,7), with all three outer vertices in the ten-site even-even class. The stated row bounds also give the same site list. Because conv(T) lies in D4, the relative closure is exactly ordinary lattice completeness in conv(T).
For two distinct lattice sites, the primitive first step along the joining segment belongs to T and differs from its starting point modulo 2. Thus a one-parity minor is a singleton.

For a least positive-area triangle in T, determinant magnitude greater than one gives a nonzero lattice representative in the half-open edge parallelogram. If its two coefficients sum to at most one, it is a nonvertex point of the triangle; otherwise reflection across the parallelogram center places it in the triangle, still a nonvertex point. Closure includes that point, and splitting at an edge or interior point produces a smaller positive-area triangle. Determinant magnitude one forces three distinct parity classes, so a two-parity set is collinear. A coordinate with nonzero primitive step is injective along the line and takes at most nine integer values in the box.

For three parities, omitting the even-even class leaves at most 21 sites. Omitting a seven-site class leaves at most 24 before closure; keeping all three even-even vertices would force T=P, so at least one further site is lost. For four parities properness bounds the size by 30.

Recomputed the four exact lower gaps from maximal sizes (1,9,23,30): 27/124, 13/62, 1/124, and 1/31. A positive common fiber area cancels from the normalized total on T; no halfspace-depth factor is asserted.

Both source candidate file hashes match. The census and full strict quota proof are in b78a2eb10bd3783f §§1–2 around (2); de93c4f08837e128 §8 restates the proper-minor consequence while distinguishing it from a quantitative bad-depth hypothesis.
